cases.name: positive control — item 1's own real span verifies
bounds: a negative start is outside the document
bounds: an end past the document is outside it
bounds: start == end is an empty span, not a resolution
floor: item 1's own opening truncated below SPAN_FLOOR
wrong region: item 1 proposed at item 2's real content
wrong region: offsets landing mid-paragraph in real prose
INV-S1: item 1 grown into item 1A's existing span
INV-S1: two sibling proposals overlapping each other
a sibling proposal duplicating another item's proposed span
shape: JSON booleans are not offsets (isinstance(True, int) is True)
shape: float offsets are not offsets

shape: a dict value is not an offset pair
shape: a 3-tuple is not an offset pair
all-or-nothing: one out-of-bounds sibling discards the good one

triage.note: D17 deliverable (a): ADR-036 §k records that `escalate.verify` — the trust boundary the whole ladder rests on — had never been handed a bad answer: both exam models answered 'cannot locate', so §b's checks were proven only against `_demo`'s constructed proposals and one 7-sub-case guards file. This battery hands the REAL verify every crafted-bad-answer class as fixture input against xom-2021's real items and real normalized_text: out-of-bounds offsets (negative, past-end, empty, inverted), sub-SPAN_FLOOR spans, plausible-but-wrong offsets at the wrong region and mid-paragraph, INV-S1 overlaps with an existing sibling and between two proposed siblings, a duplicate-sibling proposal, malformed shapes (bool/float/string/dict/3-tuple), and a mixed good+bad proposal asserting all-or-nothing. The harness additionally deep-compares the item list after every sub-case: verify must be a pure checker and the deterministic output byte-untouched. ONE GENUINE GAP found while authoring: JSON booleans pass `isinstance(v, int)` because bool subclasses int, so `[true, N]` was ACCEPTED whenever the coerced span `[1, N]` verified — probed and demonstrated against a constructed document whose body starts at offset 1, where verify returned an accepted span with `start: True`, which `apply` would have published as `"start": true` in the envelope. Fixed in the same PR by excluding bool from the shape check; the boolean sub-case here was watched red against the pre-fix tree.
triage.note_negative_space: The positive control stops the battery passing vacuously: if verify regressed to rejecting everything, it goes red. `why_contains` pins the REASON, so a class rejected only by a neighbouring check (the escalation-verify-guards provenance documents exactly that trap) is red, not accidentally green. This still says nothing about whether a real model's honest answer would ever pass verify — that needs a credential, and ADR-036 §k records where that measurement stands.

provenance: D17, created 2026-08-28 per hard rule 2. Red-first evidence in tasks/reviews/d17-red-first.txt: the boolean sub-case red against the pre-fix tree (a genuine gap — rejected on this fixture only by the accidental neighbouring similarity check, and ACCEPTED outright on the offset-1 construction now pinned in escalate._demo), and every other class proven able to fail by mutating verify (bounds check removed, SPAN_FLOOR removed, similarity removed, INV-S1 removed, pre-R2 continue restored, in-place mutation introduced) with this case red under each mutation and green on restore. Offsets are borrowed from the fixture's own envelope via like_item/shift/trunc/grow/overrun so they cannot go stale; the only literal offsets are deliberately-invalid ones.
